title: FTC probes OpenAI, Anthropic and METR — the auditor is on the list
summary: The FTC prepares civil investigative demands for OpenAI, Anthropic and the evaluator METR; Amazon and Cloudflare ship decision models built three different ways, with a model card that shows where they fail; and Claude Code's new mods let TypeScript rewire the agent from inside, unsandboxed.

topics: FTC investigation of OpenAI, Anthropic and other labs (first reported by the New York Post, 30 September 2026): civil investigative demands expected within weeks under the FTC Act's unfair-or-deceptive-practices authority; METR included because it investigated and reported on the OpenAI-Hugging Face breach (Semafor); Chairman Ferguson's stated skepticism of safety-driven regulation ('whip everyone into a panic') and the regulatory-moat suggestion; probe public a day after the White House voluntary safety accord, which Ferguson attended; an official's 'we are in the investigative phase'; lineage to the FTC's July 2023 20-page CID to OpenAI (49 inquiries, 17 document classes, 'deceptive practices relating to risks of harm to consumers')

Decision-model anatomy, after the 1 October gold rush: Amazon's Strands Decider 2B (Qwen3.5-2B torso, LM head removed for a pointer head, rank-16 LoRA, 3rd of 33 in the 2B class on JevBench, ~115 ms on an RTX 3090, ~153 ms on an M3; Brooker's 'perfect decider for a workflow step'); Cloudflare's Clef 27B and Clef-flash 9B (Apache-2.0, joint schema head scoring all options across questions after one prefill pass; BANKING77 94.2 vs Jev 79.7, BFCL 98.5 vs 95.8, GPQA Diamond 48.0 vs 78.3; Workers AI $0.24 and $0.09 per million tokens; RL fine-tuning via forward-deployed engineers); a 42-decision independent comparison (Jev 71.4% vs Clef-flash 66.7%, both 10/10 on computer-use actions); Almeida's 'cool architecture' jab; calibration claims with no shared test set

Claude Code mods (1 October 2026): in-process TypeScript/JavaScript handlers on tool, prompt and interface events that observe, rewrite or answer the event via next(); built-in features (/diff, AGENTS.md support) now ship as mods; unsandboxed, can read env vars and approve tool calls, and in auto mode a mod-approved call skips the classifier; claude plugin validate lists hooks and mods-API calls before install and unreadable API use is refused; sec-default guard on Team/Enterprise or managed machines protects deny rules, managed hooks, system prompt and managed instructions; policy mods via prependPlugins and plugin.register; process.run escapes network policy; worker crashes three times unloads non-built-in mods; settings hooks not deprecated; lineage to Emacs advice and Firefox 57's 2017 move to WebExtensions

dives.why_it_matters: Labs, evaluators and anyone shipping consumer AI now face compulsory process under deception law, and evaluators being swept in changes what third-party auditors are willing to write down.

dives.story: Three ways to build a model that only chooses
dives.why_it_matters: Agent builders choosing a cheap gating model need to know which anatomy fits and that these models fail badly where answers require knowledge rather than reading.
Daily Claude Code users and the admins who govern them now have unsandboxed in-process code that can approve tool calls, and the trust model decides whether it is safe to install any.

concepts_taught: middleware-style before/after/instead event handlers (Emacs advice lineage) and why routing every capability through one API makes a mod's permissions inspectable before install

lore.note: Alan's logging-proxy habit developed: faced with Claude Code policy mods, he objected that an audit layer that runs inside the process it polices is not the same as his proxy, whose whole point is sitting outside the thing it watches — and set a house rule that no mod which approves tool calls runs on his machine until he has read its validate output line by line.
